title: Lithium-ion duration and degradation limits
bottleneck: Lithium-ion dominates grid storage but degrades 1.5 to 3 percent per year under cycling, and stacking enough batteries for 8-plus hour duration drives capital costs above alternatives. Calendar aging, thermal management complexity, and fire risk all scale with system size. Lithium-ion is excellent for 2 to 4 hour applications and structurally unsuited for longer durations. Augmenting aging battery systems with new cells creates mismatch problems that further erode economics over a 20-year project life.
why_it_blocks: Misapplying lithium-ion to long-duration needs wastes capital. The industry's default technology cannot economically serve the fastest-growing segment of storage demand.
current_state: LFP grid batteries now claim more than 10,000 cycles with costs near 75 to 85 dollars per kWh. Durations beyond 4 hours remain uneconomic versus long-duration alternatives.
